f.title: Treat any untoward medical occurrence after exposure as an AE, whether or not causally related
f.statement: An adverse event is any untoward medical occurrence in a patient exposed to a medicinal product that does not necessarily have a causal relationship with the product; it can be any unfavourable and unintended sign (e.g. an abnormal laboratory finding), symptom or disease temporally associated with the use of the product, whether or not considered causally related.

An adverse event can therefore be any unfavourable and unintended sign (for example, an abnormal laboratory finding), symptom, or disease temporally associated with the use of a medicinal product, whether or not considered causally related to this medicinal product.

f.title: Treat spontaneously reported events as adverse drug reactions even when causality is unknown
f.statement: An adverse drug reaction is a noxious and unintended response to a medicinal product, meaning a causal relationship is at least a reasonable possibility. For regulatory reporting purposes, a spontaneously reported event meets the definition of an adverse drug reaction even if the relationship is unknown or unstated.
f.applicability: Spontaneous reports

rows.quote:
An adverse drug reaction, as defined by regional and local requirements, concerns a noxious and
unintended response to a medicinal product.

The phrase “response to a medicinal product” means that a causal relationship between a medicinal
product and an adverse event is at least a reasonable possibility. A reaction, in contrast to an event, is
characterised by the fact that a causal relationship between the medicinal product and the occurrence
is suspected. For regulatory reporting purposes, if an event is spontaneously reported, even if the
relationship is unknown or unstated, it meets the definition of an adverse drug reaction (see Section
5.1.1, AEs/ADRs).

f.title: Classify an AE/ADR as serious when it meets an ICH E2A seriousness criterion
f.statement: In accordance with ICH E2A, an AE/ADR is serious if at any dose it results in death; is life-threatening; requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongs existing hospitalisation; results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity; is a congenital anomaly/birth defect; or is an important medical event.

f.title: Consider important medical events serious based on medical and scientific judgement
f.statement: Important medical events that might not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation may be considered serious when, based on medical and scientific judgement, they might jeopardise the patient or might require intervention to prevent one of the other serious outcomes (e.g. intensive treatment in an emergency room or at home for allergic bronchospasm, blood dyscrasias or convulsions not resulting in hospitalisation, or development of dependency or substance use disorder).

hospitalisation may also be considered serious AEs/ADRs when, based on medical and scientific
judgement, they might jeopardise the patient or might require intervention to prevent one of the other
outcomes listed in the definition above. Examples of such events which may occur following the use of
a medicinal product are intensive treatment in an emergency room or at home for allergic
bronchospasm, blood dyscrasias or convulsions that do not result in hospitalisation, or development of
dependency or substance use disorder.

f.statement: PSPs are MAH-initiated ODCSs in which patients enrol to support use of the MAH’s product or management of their condition, with two-way communication between the MAH (or a third party on its behalf) and patients or HCPs. A program meets the PSP definition if it solicits medical information about the patient’s use of a product and/or its design means the MAH (or its third party) would foreseeably receive such information (e.g. HCP interaction to administer medication or provide medical advice).
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Cross-functional handoffs; Reporting policy

rows.quote:
PSPs are ODCSs initiated by an MAH, in which patients enrol for the purpose of supporting their use of
the MAH’s medicinal product, or the management of their medical condition, and which include a
mechanism for two-way communication between the MAH (or third party acting on the MAH’s behalf)
and patients or healthcare professionals. Examples of PSPs include adherence support, disease
management, and certain reimbursement and educational programs. See Section 4.5 Sources of
ICSRs, PSPs, for further details.

Programs meet the definition of a PSP if 1) they solicit medical information about the patient’s use of a
medicinal product and/or 2) the design of the program is such that the MAH (or a third party acting on
the MAH’s behalf) would foreseeably receive medical information about the patient’s use of a medicinal
product (e.g., when a program involves HCP interaction with a patient to administer medication or
provide medical advice).

rows.quote: The MAH should request and include follow-up information from the consumer or relevant HCPs as needed, seeking consent where necessary.

f.title: Understand identifiable as verified existence of a patient and a reporter
f.statement: Patient and reporter identifiability serves to avoid case duplication, ensure authenticity and facilitate follow-up; "identifiable" refers to verification of the existence of a patient and a reporter (i.e. a primary source).
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Safety intake & collection

rows.quote:
Patient and reporter identifiability is important to avoid case duplication, ensure authenticity, and
facilitate follow-up of appropriate cases. The term identifiable in this context refers to the verification
of the existence of a patient and a reporter (i.e., a primary source; see Section 2.4, Primary Source).
rows.review_note: Review: added; the definition of identifiable (6.1) determines whether the minimum criteria are met. Double-check: fixed: extended quote so it proves the whole statement. score 88: definition of identifiable; no direct duty.

f.title: Attempt to verify the patient and reporter of second-hand reports
f.statement: Second-hand reports (where the notifier lacks first-hand knowledge of the event) are considered incomplete and, where permissible and feasible, attempts should be made to verify the existence of an identifiable patient and reporter.
f.applicability: Second-hand reports

rows.quote:
Second-hand reports (i.e., situations where an individual notifies the MAH of an AE/ADR but does not
have first-hand knowledge about the event), are considered incomplete and, where permissible and
feasible, attempts should be made to verify the existence of an identifiable patient and reporter.
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: fixed: extended quote so it proves the whole statement. confirmed.

f.title: Qualify a patient as identifiable on age, sex, initials, date of birth or other identifiers
f.statement: To have an identifiable patient there should be enough information to indicate the existence of a specific patient; any one or more of age (or age category), gestational age, sex, initials, date of birth, name, patient identification number, or other identifiers specified by regional or local requirements should automatically qualify the patient as identifiable.

rows.quote: To have an identifiable patient, there should be enough information to indicate the existence of a specific patient. One or more of the following should automatically qualify a patient as identifiable: age (or age category, e.g., adolescent, adult, elderly), gestational age, sex, initials, date of birth, name, patient identification number, or other identifiers specified by regional or local requirements.

f.title: Qualify a reporter as identifiable on name, initials, address or qualification
f.statement: Characteristics that qualify a reporter as identifiable include, but are not limited to, name, initials, address (e.g. organisation, department, street, city, state or province, postcode, region or country, email, phone number) and qualification (e.g. HCP, lawyer, consumer or other non-HCP).

rows.quote: Examples of characteristics that qualify a reporter as identifiable include but are not limited to: name, initials, or address (e.g., reporter’s organisation, department, street, city, state or province, postcode, region or country, email, phone number), qualification (e.g., healthcare professional, lawyer, consumer or other non-healthcare professional).
rows.review_note: Review: Extended quote to the full list of reporter characteristics. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Report cases from anonymous reporters when the reporter's existence is known
f.statement: Where the reporter wishes to remain anonymous, the ICSR should still be reported, as long as the existence of an individual as the reporter is known and the case otherwise meets reporting requirements.

rows.quote: For cases where the reporter wishes to remain anonymous, the ICSR should still be reported, as long as the existence of an individual as the reporter is known and the case otherwise meets reporting requirements.

f.title: Do not create ICSRs for unspecified groups of patients until patient-identifiable information is obtained
f.statement: Without qualifying descriptors, a report referring to a definite number of patients (e.g. "Twenty patients experienced…" or "a few patients experienced") should not be regarded as a case until the four minimum criteria are met, and should be followed up for patient-identifiable information before an ICSR is created. To qualify for ICSR reporting it should be possible to associate the AE/ADR(s) with a specific identifiable patient.

rows.quote: In the absence of qualifying descriptors, a report referring to a definite number of patients should not be regarded as a case until the four minimum criteria for reporting are met. For example, “Twenty patients experienced…” or “a few patients experienced” should be followed up for patient-identifiable information before creating an ICSR. To qualify for ICSR reporting it should be possible to associate an AE/ADR or AEs/ADRs with a specific identifiable patient.
rows.review_note: Review: Extended quote to the follow-up and association sentences in the statement. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Do not treat a digital platform handle alone as confirming a real patient or reporter
f.statement: For digital platform cases, identifiability refers to the existence of a real person; where permissible and feasible, attempts can be made to verify the patient and reporter exist. A username or handle without qualifying identifiers is insufficient to confirm a real patient and/or reporter.
f.applicability: Cases from digital platforms
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: In relation to cases from digital platforms, the identifiability of the reporter or patient refers to the existence of a real person; where permissible and feasible, attempts can be made to verify that the patient and the reporter exist. The presence of a digital platform username or identifier (i.e., “handle”) in the absence of qualifying identifiers is insufficient to confirm that there is a real patient and/or reporter.
rows.review_note: Review: Extended quote to the real-person and verification sentence. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Accept a digital platform poster as reporter only with first-hand knowledge
f.statement: For digital platform cases, MAHs should only consider the person providing the information to qualify as a reporter if the person experienced the event or has first-hand information about it.
f.applicability: Cases from digital platforms
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: MAHs should only consider the person providing the information to qualify as a reporter if the person experienced the event or has first-hand information about it.

f.title: Seek evidence of a real patient and reporter for digital platform cases where follow-up is feasible
f.statement: Where follow-up is feasible, MAHs should attempt to obtain evidence of the existence of a real patient and reporter for digital platform cases (e.g. by requesting at least one identifiable characteristic).
f.applicability: Cases from digital platforms

rows.quote: Where follow-up is feasible, MAHs should attempt to obtain evidence of the existence of a real patient and reporter (e.g., via requesting at least one identifiable characteristic).

f.title: Write a comprehensive stand-alone narrative in the chronology of the patient's experience
f.statement: The narrative should summarise all relevant clinical and related information (patient characteristics, therapy details, medical history, concurrent conditions, clinical course, AEs/ADRs including outcome, diagnosis, laboratory evidence including normal ranges, and other information supporting causality assessment), serve as a comprehensive stand-alone "medical story", and be presented in a logical time sequence, ideally the chronology of the patient’s experience.

rows.quote: The objective of the narrative is to summarise all relevant clinical and related information, including patient characteristics, therapy details, medical history, concurrent conditions, clinical course of the event(s), AE(s)/ADR(s) including the outcome, diagnosis, laboratory evidence (including normal ranges), and any other information that supports an assessment of a causal relationship between a medicinal product and an AE/ADR. The narrative should serve as a comprehensive, stand-alone “medical story”. The information should be presented in a logical time sequence; ideally this should be presented in the chronology of the patient’s experience, rather than in the chronology in which the information was received.
rows.review_note: Review: Extended quote to the narrative content list. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Clearly identify new information in follow-up report narratives
f.statement: In follow-up reports, new information should be clearly identified.

rows.quote: In follow-up reports, new information should be clearly identified.

f.title: Avoid abbreviations and acronyms in narratives except laboratory parameters and units
f.statement: Abbreviations and acronyms should be avoided in the narrative, with the possible exception of laboratory parameters and units.

rows.quote: Abbreviations and acronyms should be avoided, with the possible exception of laboratory parameters and units.

f.title: Include key supplementary record information, note its availability and supply it on request
f.statement: Key information from supplementary records should be included in the report; its availability should be mentioned in the narrative and the appropriate ICH E2B data element, and the records supplied on request.

rows.quote: Key information from supplementary records should be included in the report, and its availability should be mentioned in the narrative and appropriate ICH E2B data element and supplied on request.

f.title: Summarise autopsy or pathology findings and provide documents where permitted
f.statement: Any relevant autopsy or pathologic findings should be summarised in the narrative, and related documents provided according to regional or local requirements and where permitted by local data privacy laws.

rows.quote: Any relevant autopsy or pathologic findings should also be summarised in the narrative and related documents should be provided according to regional or local requirements and where permitted by local data privacy laws.

f.title: Reflect narrative terms accurately in the corresponding E2B data elements
f.statement: Terms in the narrative (e.g. AEs/ADRs, indication and medical conditions) should be accurately reflected in the appropriate ICH E2B data elements.

rows.quote: Terms (e.g., AEs/ADRs, indication, and medical conditions) in the narrative should be accurately reflected in appropriate ICH E2B data elements.

f.title: Collect case information from the HCPs directly involved in the patient's care where possible
f.statement: If possible, information about the case should be collected from the HCPs directly involved in the patient’s care.

rows.quote: If possible, information about the case should be collected from the HCPs who are directly involved in the patient’s care.

f.title: Carefully review each report for accuracy and completeness of medical information
f.statement: Regardless of the source, the initial recipient should carefully review the report for accuracy and completeness of the medical information; the review should include, but is not limited to: seriousness (per Section 2.1.3); whether a diagnosis is possible and supported by evidence; whether relevant diagnostic procedures were performed; whether alternative causes and/or confounding factors were considered; information on temporal association and outcome; and what additional information is needed.

rows.quote: Regardless of the source of an AE/ADR report, the initial recipient should carefully review the report for the accuracy and completeness of the medical information. The review should include, but is not limited to, the following considerations: • Are the AE(s)/ADR(s) serious (according to the criteria in Section 2.1.3, Serious AE/ADR)? • Is a diagnosis possible from the description of the AE(s)/ADR(s) and is it supported by evidence? • Have the relevant diagnostic procedures been performed? • Were alternative causes and/or confounding factors for the AE(s)/ADR(s) considered? • Is there information regarding a temporal association between the medicinal product and the AE(s)/ADR(s), and information on the outcome? • What additional information is needed?
rows.review_note: Review: Extended quote to the review considerations; statement says "include, but is not limited to" as the source does (was "at least"). Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Seek additional information on reports, including second-hand reports
f.statement: Because initial AE/ADR reports may lack sufficient information for clinical case evaluation, efforts should be made to seek additional information, including on AEs/ADRs reported second-hand.
f.applicability: Initial and second-hand reports

rows.quote: Initial AE/ADR reports may not have sufficient information for clinical case evaluation, and efforts should be made to seek additional information on reports, including AEs/ADRs that were reported second-hand

f.title: Collect and retain patient and reporter details at initial report to enable follow-up
f.statement: At the time of the original report, sufficient details about the patient and reporter should be collected and retained to enable follow-up, within the constraints of regional or local data privacy laws.
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: It is important that at the time of the original report, sufficient details about the patient and reporter be collected and retained to enable follow-up, within the constraints imposed by regional or local data privacy laws.

f.title: Prioritise follow-up by seriousness, expectedness and special interest
f.statement: Follow-up should first be prioritised by importance: highest priority for serious unexpected cases; slightly lower for serious expected and non-serious unexpected cases. Cases of special interest (e.g. AEs/ADRs under enhanced monitoring at the request of regulatory authorities) should also be prioritised.

rows.quote:
To optimise the value of follow-up, the first consideration should be prioritisation of case reports by
importance. Highest priority for follow-up are cases which are both serious and unexpected. At a
slightly lower priority are serious, expected and non-serious, unexpected cases. In addition to

f.title: Document all follow-up requests and attempts
f.statement: All requests and attempts for follow-up information should be documented.

rows.quote: All requests and attempts for follow-up information should be documented.

f.title: Ask specific follow-up questions and tailor methods to collect missing information
f.statement: The MAH should provide the specific questions it would like answered, and follow-up methods should be tailored towards optimising collection of missing information to allow meaningful case evaluation.

rows.quote: The MAH should provide specific questions it would like to have answered. Follow-up methods should be tailored towards optimising the collection of missing information to allow meaningful case evaluation.

f.title: Use targeted questionnaires or specific forms, preferably at initial report
f.statement: Use of a targeted questionnaire or specific form is encouraged, preferably at the time of the initial report, to capture clinically relevant and complete information.

rows.quote: To facilitate the capture of clinically relevant and complete information, use of a targeted questionnaire or specific form is encouraged, preferably at the time of the initial report.

f.title: Involve staff with appropriate PV training and therapeutic expertise in follow-up
f.statement: Individuals with the appropriate level of pharmacovigilance training and therapeutic expertise should be involved in the follow-up of received cases.

rows.quote: Individuals with the appropriate level of pharmacovigilance training and therapeutic expertise should be involved in the follow-up of received cases.

f.title: Exercise caution before following up private messages on third-party digital platforms
f.statement: For cases from digital platforms not under the MAH’s responsibility, MAHs should exercise caution before following up any message marked as private, as this may breach consent depending on regional and local privacy regulations.
f.applicability: Digital platforms not under the responsibility of the MAH
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote:
In relation to cases from digital platform not under the responsibility of the MAH, MAHs should exercise
caution prior to conducting follow-up of any message marked as private, as this may constitute a
breach of consent depending on regional and local privacy regulations.
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: fixed: extended quote so it proves the whole statement. confirmed.

f.title: Follow up overdose, abuse, misuse, medication error and occupational exposure reports
f.statement: Reports of overdose, abuse, misuse, medication error and occupational exposure without an AE/ADR should be followed up to make the information as complete as possible regarding suspected drug(s) and context of occurrence.
f.clause: 6.4.1.1. Overdose, abuse, misuse, medication error and occupational exposure

rows.quote:
For some other observations without an AE/ADR, there are specific considerations for follow up as
outlined below:

6.4.1.1. Overdose, abuse, misuse, medication error and occupational exposure

Reports should be followed up to ensure that the information is as complete as possible with regard to
suspected drug(s) and the context of occurrence.
rows.location: 6.4.1.1. Overdose, abuse, misuse, medication error and occupational exposure
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: fixed: extended quote to the 6.4.1 lead-in so the "without an AE/ADR" scope is proven. confirmed.

f.title: Follow up all pregnancy reports where the embryo or foetus could have been exposed
f.statement: MAHs are expected to follow up all pregnancy reports from HCPs or consumers where the embryo or foetus could have been exposed (through maternal or paternal exposure) to one of its products; for certain products, potential embryo-foetal exposure may need to be considered even if the product was taken before the gestational period commenced.
f.clause: 6.4.1.2. Exposure to medicinal products associated with pregnancy or breastfeeding
f.exceptions: Not expected for exposure during pregnancy for products specifically indicated for use in pregnancy if not associated with an AE/ADR.

rows.quote:
MAHs are expected to follow up all pregnancy reports from HCPs or consumers where the embryo or
foetus could have been exposed (through maternal or paternal exposure) to one of its medicinal
products. For certain types of medicinal products, potential for embryo-foetal exposure may need to be
considered even if the medicinal product was taken before the gestational period commenced. MAHs
should collect information on the outcome of the pregnancy, health of the newborn, and, where
appropriate, development of the child. This follow up is not expected for cases of exposure during
pregnancy for products specifically indicated for use during pregnancy if not associated with an
AE/ADR.
rows.location: 6.4.1.2. Exposure to medicinal products associated with pregnancy or breastfeeding

f.title: Collect pregnancy outcome, newborn health and child development information
f.statement: MAHs should collect information on the outcome of the pregnancy, the health of the newborn and, where appropriate, development of the child. This follow-up is not expected for exposure during pregnancy for products specifically indicated for use during pregnancy if not associated with an AE/ADR.
f.clause: 6.4.1.2. Exposure to medicinal products associated with pregnancy or breastfeeding
f.exceptions: Not expected for products specifically indicated for use during pregnancy if not associated with an AE/ADR.

f.title: Specify ICSR exchange, timelines and reporting responsibilities in agreements
f.statement: Contractual agreements between MAHs and third parties (e.g. service providers who would foreseeably receive safety information) or other marketing companies should specify the management and reporting of ICSRs, i.e. processes for exchange of safety information including timelines and regulatory reporting responsibilities, in accordance with regional and local requirements.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder and contractual partners
rows.quote:
Contractual agreements may take place between MAHs and third parties (e.g., service providers) who
perform activities for the MAH in which they would foreseeably receive or otherwise obtain safety
information associated with the MAH’s medicinal product. Further, the marketing of medicines may
take place through contractual agreements between MAHs and other companies, which may market
one or more products with the same active substance name in the same or different regions or
countries.

It is important that these agreements specify the management and reporting of ICSRs (i.e., processes
for exchange of safety information, including timelines and regulatory reporting responsibilities) in
accordance with regional and local requirements.
rows.review_note: Review: Processes: replaced intake with reg-reporting (agreements fix reporting responsibilities). Double-check: fixed: extended quote to the agreement types named in the statement. confirmed.

f.title: Have processes to identify responsibilities and avoid duplicate reporting between partners
f.statement: Processes should be in place to identify responsibilities, as applicable, and avoid duplicate reporting to regulatory authorities.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder and contractual partners
rows.quote: Processes should be in place to identify responsibilities, as applicable, and avoid duplicate reporting to regulatory authorities.

f.title: Retain ultimate MAH responsibility for reporting within required timelines
f.statement: Whatever the nature of the agreements, the MAH is ultimately responsible for reporting within the required timelines.
f.processes: Partner & vendor oversight; Submission operations; Reporting policy

rows.quote: Whatever the nature of the agreements, the MAH is ultimately responsible for reporting within the required timelines

f.statement: Contractual partners should minimise the data exchange period to enable compliance with MAH reporting responsibilities.
f.processes: Partner & vendor oversight; Safety intake & collection

rows.quote: the contractual partners should minimise the data exchange period to enable compliance with MAH responsibilities

f.title: Consider and manage duplicates when reviewing pharmacovigilance data
f.statement: Regulatory authorities and MAHs should consider and manage duplicate reports when reviewing pharmacovigilance data, as duplicates negatively impact signal detection.
f.processes: ICSR quality control; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: Regulatory Authorities and MAHs should consider and manage duplicates when reviewing pharmacovigilance data, as duplicates negatively impact signal detection.

f.title: Use suitable duplicate management strategies and E2B duplicate actions
f.statement: MAHs may use the duplicate management strategies most suitable for their situation. ICH E2B supports actions upon detection of duplicates, i.e. populating E2B data elements with other case identification numbers by which the case is known and submitting nullification or amendment reports as applicable.
f.processes: ICSR quality control; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote:
MAHs may utilise duplicate management strategies that are most suitable for their individual situation.
ICH E2B supports specific actions to be taken upon detection of duplicates (i.e., population of ICH E2B
data elements with other case identification numbers by which the case is known and submission of
nullification or amendment reports as applicable).
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: fixed: extended quote so it proves the whole statement. confirmed.

f.title: Allow for differing reporter information when detecting duplicates
f.statement: Duplicate detection relies on good quality data and is generally based on similarities, but should take into account that information in ICSRs may differ between reporters.
f.processes: ICSR quality control; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: Duplicate detection relies on good quality data and is generally based on similarities but should take into account that information in ICSRs may differ between reporters.

f.title: Transmit ICSRs electronically in ICH E2B format
f.statement: ICSRs should be transmitted electronically using the ICH E2B format, according to the ICH E2B guidelines.

rows.quote: ICSRs should be transmitted electronically using the ICH E2B format, according to the ICH E2B guidelines.

f.title: Use other formats such as CIOMS I where ICH E2B is not yet implemented
f.statement: In regions or countries where ICH E2B has yet to be implemented, other formats (e.g. CIOMS I) may be used.
f.applicability: Regions or countries where ICH E2B is not implemented

rows.quote: In regions or countries where ICH E2B has yet to be implemented, other formats (e.g., CIOMS I) may be utilised.
